description: Returns change history for a specific entity

parameters.name: entity_type
parameters.description: The type of entity to retrieve change history for

parameters.name: entity_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the entity to retrieve change history for

parameters.name: filters[changed_by]
parameters.description: Filter by user who made the change

parameters.name: filters[changed_at]
parameters.description: Changed at filter (date range format: YYYY-MM-DD...YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ...YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ)

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sorting criteria in minus-based order format. Default sort order is ascending. Prefix with minus (-) for descending order. Default sort is by changed_at in descending order. Supports both snake_cas...

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: The number of items per page to be returned

parameters.name: Accept-Language
parameters.description: Locale for localized response messages (for example: en, fr-FR, pseudo)

200.description: Change history records retrieved successfully. Response varies based on entity_type.

400.description: The server could not understand the request due to invalid syntax or parameters that fail to meet validation requirements.

401.description: Although the HTTP standard specifies "unauthorized", semantically this response means "unauthenticated". That is, the client must authenticate itself to get the requested response.

403.description: The client does not have access rights to the content; that is, it is authenticated, but the server is refusing to give the requested resource. Unlike 401, the client's identity is known to the server.

404.description: The server can not find the requested resource. This can mean either the URL is not recognized, or the resource itself does not exist. Servers may also send this response instead of 403 to hide the existence of a resource from an unauthorized client.
